The starter templates are offered when you create a new template (for example Air-Brake Inspection and Trailer Inspection).
steps: Go to Settings > Inspection Templates and create a new template.
Choose to start from a template and pick a starter (for example Air-Brake Inspection).
Select a checkbox field that came with the starter.
Read the 'Note required if Monitor / Not OK' option in its properties.
Read the 'Photo required if Not OK' option in its properties.

ready.title: Completing a reopened inspection again gives the report a new inspected date
ready.why_needed: New in the spec: the inspected date is the first completion date and only reopening and completing again gives a new date; the updated regenerate case checks that regenerating keeps the date, but nothing checks that completing again changes it.

rules.entry: Developer and QA questions answered

preconditions: You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - View'.

A completed inspection on an open work order, with its report, first completed at least one day before you run this test (for example yesterday). A completion date cannot be set by hand, so the inspection must be completed on an earlier day.
steps: Open the inspection's report and note the inspected date.
Open the completed inspection and reopen it.
Change one answer.
Press 'Submit & Generate Report' and finish the sign-off.
Open the newest report from the inspection report note on the work order.
Read the inspected date.
expected: Step 1: the inspected date is the day the inspection was first completed (for example yesterday).
Step 6: the newest report shows today's date as the inspected date, so it can be told apart from the earlier version.
ready.notes: Verdict KEEP. Small note applied: the inspection must be completed at least a day before the run, because a tester cannot back-date a completion. The reopen-gives-new-date half may be how the product already behaved, but it was never written down before 5 Oct, so it is a spec addition with no case. No ShopCoach needed.

ready.title: Changing or merging the asset does not regenerate the inspection report
ready.why_needed: The PM decided on 8 Oct, after the spec, that an asset change or merge never regenerates existing reports and that a manual regenerate takes the work order's current asset with the inspected date unchanged; this is not yet in the PRD and no case checks it, so a build that silently regenerates would pass.

rules.entry: Milos Vasic (PM) in Jira; not yet in PRD v43 ('I'll add this to the PRD')
Developer and QA questions answered (the inspected date the PM's ruling refers to)

preconditions: You are signed in with 'Work orders - Create & Edit' and 'Customers - View', and you can edit the customer's assets.
You can regenerate an inspection report. No source names the regenerate control or the role that grants it: read both off the build and write them here before running.
A customer with three assets: asset A (for example unit 1001), asset B (for example unit 2002) and asset C (for example unit 3003). Asset C has a VIN; write it down.
An open work order on asset A with a completed inspection and its report, first completed at least one day before you run this test (for example yesterday).
steps: Open the report from the inspection report note on the work order and note the asset and the inspected date it shows.
On the work order, change the asset from asset A to asset B and save.
Open the report from the inspection report note again.
Regenerate the report.
Open the report from the inspection report note.
Open asset B, change its VIN to asset C's VIN, save, and answer Yes to 'Would you like to merge with the already existing asset?'.
Open the report from the inspection report note again.
expected: Step 1: the report shows asset A and the inspected date (for example yesterday's date).
Step 3: the report still shows asset A; changing the work order's asset did not change it.
Step 5: the report now shows asset B, the work order's current asset.
Step 5: the inspected date is the same as in step 1.
Step 7: the report still shows asset B, as in step 5; the merge did not change it.
ready.notes: Verdict FIX, every correction applied: the asset-edit right is added (step 6 edits a VIN and confirms the merge, which 'Customers - View' alone cannot do); the regenerate control and the role that grants it are left for the build to name, because the spec names neither and no permission is invented; asset C's VIN is a precondition; step 3 now checks only what the report shows (a tester cannot see a version list, and the spec does not say where earlier versions are listed). Divergence to disclose in the case: this rests on Milos Vasic's SV-10960 ruling of 8 Oct, which he said he would add to the PRD; v43 (13 Oct) does not carry it. The merge route (VIN edit, answer Yes) is the one documented on SV-10965 (Stefan Vukovic, 8 Oct, step 9). Shares its source with 'A kept inspection follows its work order's asset at deletion and on merge'.

ready.title: A new work order stays, empty, when its drafting is cancelled
ready.why_needed: New in the spec: a new work order is created as soon as it is chosen and stays, empty, when drafting is cancelled or the user leaves; nothing is deleted automatically. 'The inspection stays needing action' and 'no build note is written' were already 22 Sep behaviour (a drafted-then-abandoned build leaves the findings unactioned; the note is written only when lines land) and are re-checked here only because they sit in the same flow. The existing cases check cancelling only on the inspection's own work order, never on a new one.

rules.entry: Not named in the change log; written into the PRD by Milos Vasic (PM); Jira SV-10792 (2 Oct 2026) already quotes the new text

preconditions: The shop has ShopCoach and at least one labor type.
You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit', 'Work orders - Create & Edit', 'Customers - View' and 'Work orders - View'.
A completed inspection with a Not OK finding that you completed on this build and that has not been built from, so its row on the asset's Inspections tab offers the build action.
steps: Open the completed inspection.
Press Build lines and choose A new work order.
Note the new work order's number (for example S1-2301).
While the lines are still drafting, press Cancel.
Open the new work order's Lines tab and Notes tab.
Open the asset's Inspections tab and find the inspection's row.
Open the completed inspection again.
expected: Step 2: the new work order is created at once and you land on its Lines tab.
Step 5: the new work order still exists, with no lines added; it was not deleted.
Step 5: there is no note saying lines were built from the inspection.
Step 6: the row still offers the build action and is counted in 'N of M have findings with no lines yet'.
Step 7: the completed inspection still offers Build lines.
ready.notes: Verdict FIX, every correction applied. The retry step is removed from the manual test: 'a retry runs on the same work order' needs a drafting failure, which cannot be forced by hand, so it needs automation (AUTOMATION: HOLD - drafting failure cannot be forced by hand). why_needed now separates the 22 Sep behaviour from the new part. If the drafting finishes before you can press Cancel, start again with a fresh inspection; the rule also covers leaving the page while drafting runs. Needs a working ShopCoach build flow: run on Staging (the QA environment is blocked for this, SV-11084).

preconditions: The shop has ShopCoach and at least one labor type.
You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit'.
A template with two checkbox fields (for example Wipers and Lights). On Lights, 'Note required if Monitor / Not OK' is turned off.

An inspection from that template on an open work order, completed with: Wipers answered Not OK, with the note 'Left wiper blade torn' and a photo of something else (for example a cracked mirror); and Lights answered Not OK, with a photo of something distinctive (for example a flat tire) and no note.
steps: Open the completed inspection.
Press Build lines and choose This work order.
Wait for the proposed lines.
Read the proposed line for Wipers.
Read the proposed line for Lights.
expected: Step 4: the Wipers line is about the torn wiper blade from the note; it does not mention the cracked mirror, which is only in the photo.

The expectation may move: the S15 status panel in PRD v43 says the Key Decisions on the brief are provisional and that, until the new inspection line builder lands, builds use the existing ShopCoach line builder assistant; the photo decision is one of them. preconditions: You are signed in with 'Customers - View', 'Work orders - View' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', and you can delete work orders and edit assets.
A customer with three assets: asset A (for example unit 1001), asset B (for example unit 2002) and asset C (for example unit 3003). Asset C has a VIN; write it down.
A work order on asset A with a completed inspection and its report; one answer in it carries a photo.
steps: On the work order, change the asset from asset A to asset B and save.
Delete the work order.
Open asset B's Inspections tab.
Open asset A's Inspections tab.
On asset B's tab, open the kept inspection and look at the answer that had a photo.
Open asset B, change its VIN to asset C's VIN, save, and answer Yes to 'Would you like to merge with the already existing asset?'.
Open asset C's Inspections tab.
expected: Step 3: the inspection is listed on asset B, the asset the work order had when it was deleted, with a dash in the Work order column.
Step 4: the inspection is not listed on asset A.

Latest wins, so the case follows the ruling; ask the PM to update S5-R21. Expected step 7 now names the asset that survives the merge. rules.entry: QA contradiction pass answered (Milos Vasic, PM: 'Reference files open for anyone who can view the inspection.')
QA contradiction pass answered (Milos Vasic, PM)

preconditions: A published template with a checkbox field (for example Brakes) that carries a general reference file (for example brake-procedure.pdf) and, with 'Add follow-up to a response' on, a Not OK follow-up with an attached file (for example adjust-slack.pdf).
The template is added to a line on an open work order, and the inspection is not yet submitted.
A user whose role does not include 'Work orders - View'. Set the role under Settings - Staff / Roles.
Check before running: signed in as that user, you can reach and open the inspection. If you cannot, stop: this test cannot be run on this build. Report it to the QA lead.
steps: Sign in as that user and open the inspection.
Click the reference file's name on Brakes.
Close the viewer.
Answer Brakes Not OK.
Click the follow-up file's name.
expected: Step 2: the reference file opens in the viewer, although the user does not have 'Work orders - View'.
Step 5: the follow-up file opens in the viewer, although the user does not have 'Work orders - View'.
ready.notes: Verdict FIX, correction applied: the earlier role example ('a technician role with Work Order Lines - Create & Edit only') was an assumption, not a source fact, and is removed. Before this test ships, prove on the build that a user without 'Work orders - View' can reach and open an inspection at all (inspections are opened from a work order's line; the spec names no route that avoids viewing the work order). If no such user can open an inspection, the precondition is unreachable and the change has nothing a tester can observe: drop the test and tell the QA lead. Answering Not OK without submitting is fine even with the default note rule on. File names are links, with no separate Open or View button.

needs_product.title: Split line with an inspection: the moved note offers Build lines
needs_product.question: When a work order line that carries a completed inspection is split onto a new work order, its inspection report note moves to the new work order. After that: (1) Should the moved note offer Build lines, when the inspection has a Monitor or Not OK finding and has not been built from? (2) Should View PDF and Download on the moved note open and download the report? (3) Should the asset's Inspections tab show the new work order in the inspection's Work order column and link to it? In short: after a split, which work order counts as the one the inspection was run on?
needs_product.source_says: PRD v43 S7-E4 (6 Oct): "The inspection's report notes are not records of the build: when a line with an inspection is split onto a new work order, those notes move with the line and are removed from the original. Work orders split before this rule keep their notes where they are." Milos Vasic on SV-10913 (6 Oct) confirmed only that the notes move with the line and are removed from the old work order. Build lines on the moved note, working View PDF/Download and the asset row linking to the new work order come from Viktoria Videnovic's proposal (items 3-4) and Stefan Vukovic's (developer) ready-for-QA notes of 7 Oct; the PM did not answer those points. The note move itself is already covered by the planned update of C88540 and is not repeated here. Partly arguable from S4-R1 and S5-R21, but neither says which work order the inspection was 'run on' after a split.

needs_product.source_says: PRD v43 S15-R13: "Each proposed line will name the finding it came from"; S15-R21: "Each proposed line will carry the identifier of the finding it came from"; Key Decision: "No empty lines are created. There is no non-AI line builder to fall back to." S15-R14 / S2-E3 (every flagged finding represented by at least one line; a large set is split, not dropped) are unchanged since 22 Sep and already covered by C88518 and C88544.
